newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds little changed, unimpressed by budget.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds little changed, unimpressed by budget.

text.p: Irish bonds were unimpressed by a budget package that offered few surprises, dealers said on Wednesday.
The 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was yielding 5.77 percent by 1445 GMT on Wednesday, having edged up from 5.74 earlier in the session but below the 5.81 percent it traded at late on Tuesday.
The benchmark 8.0 percent stock due 2006 also eased, its yield creeping out to 6.53 from 6.50 percent earlier.
"There has been no reaction in the bond market. It was virtually all leaked beforehand and most of the forecasts were much as expected," one dealer said.

Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn set a 1997 Exchequer borrowing target of 637 million Irish pounds or 1.6 percent of GNP, slightly lower than some market forecasts, which had ranged from 585 million to 755 million punts.
"That is reasonably comforting but the Irish bond market is really keying off international events, particularly currency developments in the EMS grid," the dealer added.
